Prevention: December, collect all fallen leaves, and small bushes of grape and destroy outside the field.
They may host the disease on them between seasons
Sterilise the equipment well before and after the pruning, by using washing up liquid or detol liquid
Make sure the field is not too humid, as the disease can spread like this
Balanced fertiliser to keep the plants healthy and vigorous so that they can fight the disease if it comes
Monitoring: March, check the field every week for the onset of the disease
Look for the disease on the leaves and fruits.
Symptoms are: death or blackening of the stem or shoot, brown spotting and yellowish-green tips of the leaves.
Grapes may exhibit fungal white or orange brown hairs or structures appearing as a white to gray coat on the leaf
If crop is infected, act quickly so that the disease does not spread in the field
